phases.name: Foundations
phases.intro: The ground everything else stands on. Most of it changes nothing on screen, but it fixes how game code is written, which is why it comes before the UI.

phases.name: Features
phases.intro: What games use. Menus, gamepad, prefabs and the component kit show up here, and the acceptance game is built alongside in its own repository. Cards with touch points and checks are written at the frame-loop gate.

phases.name: Release
phases.intro: Measure, freeze the API, fix what's over budget, ship release candidates, tag 1.0.

groups.name: Kickoff
groups.note: 0.40 lands, the definition gate settles what 1.0 means, and the plans get ready for Phase 5.

groups.name: Track A · Foundations
groups.note: Independent of the frame-loop gate, in this order.

groups.name: Track B · Experiments
groups.note: Evidence for the gates; nothing merges.

groups.name: Track A · Beside the experiments
groups.note: W8a and the M0b–R2 pair run while the experiments wait for their gate (implementation plan §6).

groups.name: Gates
groups.note: The decisions Track C builds on.

groups.name: Track C · Shape of game code
Close-out
groups.note: The Phase 5 audit, then the first UI on screen.

groups.name: Data and gameplay
groups.note: Scene components, physics gaps, the kit and prefabs.

groups.name: UI, settings and input
groups.note: Persisted settings and save slots, world labels with the gamepad, controls, menus, debug views.

groups.name: Audio and shipping
groups.note: Buses and layers, the CLI, examples, conditional threading work.

groups.name: Close-out
groups.note: The Phase 6 audit and the feature gate.

groups.name: Measure and freeze
groups.note: Budgets, then the public API is final.

groups.name: Tune and ship
groups.note: Performance, platforms, release candidates, the tag.

stops.title: QA and cleanup pass
stops.summary: The QA and cleanup pass, the B1–B8 fixes and the 1.0 planning drafts. The last release before 1.0 work starts.

stops.title: Definition gate
stops.summary: Settled what 1.0 means: a complete, stable engine tested by one acceptance game, a top-down survivors-like auto-shooter. wgpu and winit types stay out of the public API; gamepad, save slots, sliders and checkboxes are in; the render thread moved to 1.x.

stops.label: Step 0
stops.title: Graduation, amendment folds and Step 0
stops.summary: The definition gate's follow-ups: the new commit rule is recorded, W4, W9, W11, W12 and W14 graduate with their amendments folded in, the remaining amendments are folded, then Step 0 readies the repository for milestone plans.
stops.note: No milestone plan: Step 0 is the tooling every later plan needs. Items 0b and 0d stop for your answer.

stops.label: W14a
stops.title: Headless test harness
stops.summary: Tests drive the real frame loop without opening a window, so example 01's tests stop copying the loop by hand. Every later test, the UI's included, builds on it.

stops.label: W2 R0
stops.title: Sprite IDs become numbers
stops.summary: Games name sprites through interned IDs instead of strings, which speeds up the extract. Every example's sprite IDs change.

stops.label: W1 M0a
stops.title: Text engine split
stops.summary: Text layout moves out of the GPU code. Alignment, wrapping, ellipsis and measuring become reachable. Nothing changes on screen.
stops.note: Runs in Track A: the definition gate moved the render thread to 1.x (Q4, D-102).

stops.label: W11a with W7a
stops.title: Logs and crash reports
stops.summary: Each game gets a user folder with a log file, and a crash writes a report there. Windows builds stop opening a console window.
stops.note: Your check: a crash file from a shipped Linux archive, and the Windows console if you have a Windows machine.

stops.label: W9a with W12a
stops.title: Licence notices and a game outside this repository
stops.summary: Release archives carry the third-party licence notices, the embedded font's included. Then templates/basic appears, and a copy of it builds and runs from any folder; until now every example has had to run from the repository root.
stops.note: W9a's steps run first (D-108). Your check: read the notices in a rehearsal archive. The skeleton registers engine systems by hand until W15a removes them; the getting-started guide starts here as W9b's first draft.

stops.label: W1 M1
stops.title: Core UI model
stops.summary: Layout, focus and hit testing, tested headless. Nothing draws yet.

stops.label: Track B
stops.title: Frame-loop experiments
stops.summary: Trial runs in a scratch copy: parallel extract, tuple queries, the fixed-step and clock design, and the glyph path. Nothing merges. The results go to the next gate.
stops.note: Runs unattended while you're disconnected.

stops.label: W8a
stops.title: Engine bug fixes
stops.summary: Burst emitters respect once, tilemaps stop covering sprites under GPU depth, an unknown sprite ID warns instead of silently drawing nothing, and render errors are returned instead of only logged.

stops.label: W1 M0b with W2 R2
stops.title: Input groundwork and render work before the swapchain wait
stops.summary: Keys stop sticking after an alt-tab; Home, End, Delete, Page Up and Page Down become real keys, and modifiers are tracked. Then the scene and post passes are recorded before the engine waits for the next screen image, judged on frame time.
stops.note: R2's perf baseline is taken after M0b's steps; the pair splits if winit 0.31 has left prerelease when the plan is written (D-108). Your check: an alt-tab on the reference machine. Perf captures run while you're disconnected from NoMachine.

stops.title: Glyph gate and frame-loop gate
stops.summary: You confirm the W6 and W13 tiers proposed from the acceptance game's agreed spec, then choose how glyphs are drawn (its damage numbers ask for per-glyph effects), how the frame loop and its stages work, how threads are used, and what keeps running while the game is paused.
stops.gate: glyph gate and the frame-loop gate

stops.label: W15a
stops.title: Stages and plugins
stops.summary: A game's main.rs stops listing engine systems in order. Systems go into named stages, and the engine arrives as one plugin set.
stops.note: The acceptance game's repository starts here and grows through Phase 6.

stops.label: W3a
stops.title: Game clock and timers
stops.summary: Pause, time scale and frame count come from the engine, and a Timer type replaces hand-counted cooldowns.

stops.label: W15b
stops.title: Tuple queries and bundles
stops.summary: Game code gets shorter: one query in place of collect-then-get, one spawn in place of the platformer player's 11 inserts.

stops.label: W3b
stops.title: Fixed step with interpolation
stops.summary: Physics runs at a fixed rate and drawing interpolates between steps, so motion stays smooth at uneven frame rates.

stops.label: W15c
stops.title: Extracts that add up
stops.summary: Tilemaps draw through the default extract. A game adds its own extract beside it instead of replacing it.

stops.label: Phase 5 QA pass
stops.title: Phase 5 audit
stops.summary: An audit of everything Phase 5 changed, in the same shape as the 0.40 pass, before Phase 6 builds on it.

stops.label: W1 M2
stops.title: First UI on screen
stops.summary: Panels, text, images and nine-slices draw in the final pass, shown in a new UI fixture example, with a hot-reloaded theme and a layout-bounds overlay.
stops.note: May run on into Phase 6.

stops.label: W1 M3
stops.title: UI input routing
stops.summary: UI sees input before gameplay: ui_* actions, focus and keyboard navigation, and a routed gameplay view so a click on a button doesn't also land in the game.

stops.label: W16a
stops.title: Components in scene files
stops.summary: Scene files can place physics bodies, lights and a game's own components, not only sprites.

stops.label: W6a
stops.title: Kinematic bodies, sensors, ray queries
stops.summary: Kinematic bodies for the player's mover, sensors for projectiles, pickups and contact damage, and the shape query that finds the nearest enemy.

stops.label: W13a and W13b
stops.title: Kit basics and parent–child transforms
stops.summary: Animated sprites, lifetimes, despawn outside a region or the view, a sound on an event and the cursor in world space come from tungsten-kit instead of example code; children follow their parents.

stops.label: W16b
stops.title: Prefabs and Tiled objects
stops.summary: Projectiles and enemies spawn from prefab files; Tiled object classes and the kit's spawner place them.

stops.label: W13c and W13d
stops.title: Controllers and gameplay helpers
stops.summary: The top-down mover the acceptance game uses and the platformer controller for example 01 (ground check, coyote time, jump buffer, variable jump), plus health with a hit flash, trigger zones, a path follower and a per-entity state machine.

stops.label: W11b and W11c
stops.title: Settings and save slots
stops.summary: Volume, display and key bindings survive a restart, a corrupt settings file has a defined fallback, and unlocks and best records persist in a save slot that loads back after its format changes.
stops.note: One candidate since 0.66: save slots (in by Q16 at the definition gate, D-102) need only the settings' atomic write.

stops.label: W1 WL with W5a
stops.title: Damage numbers, name tags and gamepad
stops.summary: Short-lived text placed in the world: damage numbers that pop and scale as a whole, name tags over heads, culled and capped each frame, drawn under the UI. Then play and navigate menus with a controller.
stops.note: Placed at the frame-loop gate (D-126, D-132) for the acceptance game's damage numbers; glyphon draws them, so they animate per label. W5a pairs with it since 0.66 (D-108), so the gamepad lands before M4's playthrough; it is in by Q9 (D-102). Your check: a gamepad on the reference machine.

stops.label: W1 BC
stops.title: Sliders, checkboxes, scroll containers
stops.summary: The broader controls a settings screen needs.
stops.note: In, by Q8 at the definition gate (D-102).

stops.label: W1 M4
stops.title: Menus you can use
stops.summary: A pause menu, HUD and settings screen you navigate with the keyboard, with screen transitions.

stops.label: W1 M5
stops.title: Debug views in the new UI
stops.summary: The HUD, timing overlay and inspector become movable windows, with a log console and a frame-time graph.

stops.label: W1 M5 polish
stops.title: Debug views you can read
stops.summary: The debug windows at a readable size on any display, docked so their defaults never overlap, in a dark look whose colours mean something, with zoom keys and new columns.
stops.note: The owner's request of 2026-10-15, after M57; no implementation-plan card.

stops.label: UI lab reference and QA
stops.title: A UI lab to copy from
stops.summary: A QA pass over the UI work since M54, windowed mode that keeps its size through resizes and fullscreen switches, and the UI lab reworked into a reference: documented modules, an inventory screen, shorter transitions and one aligned theme.
stops.note: The owner's request of 2026-10-15, after M58; no implementation-plan card.

stops.label: W13e
stops.title: Core events and ownership
stops.summary: An event cursor that reads each event once from any stage, and spawn inheritance so that what a spawner creates leaves with its state; the sound-on-event item moves onto the cursor.
stops.note: The kit catalogue's F1 (w13-kit.md), registered by the finalizing review of 2026-10-16. Changes ECS events, so every CPU row is captured.

stops.label: W13f
stops.title: Core data assets
stops.summary: A data section in the manifest for shared definitions by kind and ID, referenced by ID or written inline, checked against every other asset at load and hot-reloaded for later reads.
stops.note: The kit catalogue's F2 (w13-kit.md). The load becomes two-phase, so a prefab can name another prefab or a data entry and be checked at load.

stops.label: W13g
stops.title: Kit foundations
stops.summary: Tags and tag filters, phase anchors, a zone and a source, scene components for every existing item, action input and a camera target, inspector rows and field descriptions under the API check, the recipe harness and genre fixtures; the template's player becomes a prefab with no game Rust.
stops.note: The kit catalogue's F3 (w13-kit.md). Recipes in two genres replace "has a user" as the admission rule from here on.

stops.label: W13h
stops.title: Stats and cues
stops.summary: Stats with ordered modifiers, and cues: reactions to kit events written in a prefab or as tag-filtered rules, with sounds, labels, spawns, counters and flags; cooldowns, counters, flags, a seeded kit random stream and an event trace.
stops.note: The kit catalogue's A (w13-kit.md). One cue rule shows every enemy's damage numbers and counts every kill, with no field on each prefab.

stops.label: W13i
stops.title: Motion and facing
stops.summary: Linear motion, follow, orbit, oscillation, facing, speed limits, wrapping, staying in view, knockback, steering and aiming, plus an animator driven by motion state and a depth sort from height.
stops.note: The kit catalogue's M (w13-kit.md). Motion writes a body's velocity or a bodiless entity's position, never a transform the sync owns.

stops.label: W13j
stops.title: Overlap and damage
stops.summary: Hitboxes and hurtboxes on a kit-owned grid, a damage pipeline with sources, tags, resistances, shields, heals and a death policy, contact damage, projectiles, pickups with a magnet and drops rolled from loot tables.
stops.note: The kit catalogue's C (w13-kit.md). Its plan opens with the grid and damage pipeline sketch.

stops.label: W13 damage types
stops.title: Damage types
stops.summary: Damage types a game declares in data: hits made of typed parts that convert, penetrate and meet resistances per type, resistances that effects can modify, events that carry the types, cue rules that filter on them and labels styled per type.
stops.note: The owner's request of 2026-10-17, after M65: the kit catalogue's DT (w13-kit.md), between C and E. The kit names no damage type; E's ailments build on its kinds.

stops.label: W13k
stops.title: Effects and abilities
stops.summary: Timed, periodic and stacking effects that modify stats and grant tags; abilities triggered by action, interval or event with costs, cooldowns, charges, targeting and payloads; levels with an xp curve and offers; ailments that build up from typed hits and apply effects.
stops.note: The kit catalogue's E (w13-kit.md), the largest API of the program; its plan opens with the effect and ability sketch. Its ailment ladders build on W13 damage types' kinds (amended 2026-10-18). W12b follows it.

stops.label: W6b and W6c
stops.title: Collision layers and audio buses
stops.summary: Separate music and effects volume, a music change for the boss, pause and fades; collision layers and masks.
stops.note: Separate volumes in the settings screen make W6c Must; layers are cut to what the game asks for.

stops.label: W14b
stops.title: Project command line
stops.summary: tungsten new starts a game from the template, tungsten check validates it, and tungsten package builds a release archive.

stops.label: W12 shell
stops.title: A template to start every game from
stops.summary: The template becomes a springboard: a shell each new game copies (title, pause, tabbed settings with display options, keybindings, gameplay options, save and load over an autosave and three slots, game over, confirm dialogs, toasts and a HUD, in a dark, square theme), a sample game to delete, and a save seam; the engine gains an exit request with a last frame for quit and close, and a frame-rate limit in the player's settings.
stops.note: The owner's request of 2026-10-19, before W12b moves the examples onto the template; no implementation-plan card. Adds a check to the frame loop, so every CPU row is captured.

stops.label: Template audit
stops.title: Template audit
stops.summary: An audit of every file in the template and the guide's template sections for correctness and for use as a reference, its fixes as numbered steps, and a cold start: a fresh session deletes the sample and builds a small game from the template and the guide alone.
stops.note: The owner's request of 2026-10-19, after the W12 shell; scope and stop condition in w12-template.md's follow-ups.

stops.label: Example fixtures
stops.title: Example fixtures in one test crate
stops.summary: Examples 03, 04 and 05 stop being demos: their pixel, transition and UI fixtures, with example 01's lighting fixture, move into one test-only crate that games never copy, and the three examples and the showcase go. The template's shell becomes the only UI reference.
stops.note: The owner's decision of 2026-10-20 (D-193). If the merged crate draws a different frame, the owner recaptures the two UI fixture images on the reference machine.

stops.label: 01 (a) rebuild
stops.title: Example 01 rebuilt on the template
stops.summary: Example 01 starts again as a sandbox on the template: the shell copied unchanged, the player on the kit's platformer controller and the moving platforms on its path follower, ten spells on one bar paid in mana, health and mana bars, an autosave on entering each area, and saves of the whole game state.
stops.note: The owner's decision of 2026-10-20 (D-194), with the design in example-01-design.md; carries W12b's Must scope and W1 M6. Kit steps: a periodic effect that restores a stat, effects paused by a tag, and exact saves for the controller and the path follower; the template's autosave requests wait until a capture succeeds.

stops.label: Template final pass
stops.title: Template final pass
stops.summary: The template's last pass before example 01 grows: no dying again right after a load, toggles that take the first click, three rotating autosaves you can turn off, a question before an older save loads, a clearer save screen, bloom, the UI at 75 % by default, a smaller outlined slider thumb, Uncapped with a 60 fps floor, a Dark Souls-style game over over a pixelating world, a black play area, an enemy that stands still and a Windows icon; then every maintained doc brought up to date.
stops.note: The owner's request of 2026-10-20, after 01 (a) and before 01 (b); level C for letter spacing on UI text. Example 01 copies each shell change in the same step, and the shell-copy check covers the theme file.

stops.label: 01 (b) elements and weapons
stops.title: Elements and weapons
stops.summary: Physical, fire, cold and shock damage with crits; freezing, burning and shock with the chain reactions between them, rolling through a pile a step at a time; lightning from the sky that jumps along iron; a gun with a magazine; damage numbers and a training dummy to try it all on.
stops.note: Design in example-01-design.md; the milestone writes its own decision. Kit step: an effect keeps its source through a save.

stops.label: 01 (c) bestiary
stops.title: Bestiary
stops.summary: Five enemies that patrol, spot the player, chase, search and return: a fire wisp, a frost crawler, an iron beetle, a dive bat and a troll that throws what it picks up, each with its own resistances; difficulty scales their health and damage; health and mana drops and a combat music layer.
stops.note: Design in example-01-design.md; the milestone writes its own decision. Kit steps: hitboxes' hit lists and state machines survive a save.

stops.label: 01 (d) new level
stops.title: A new level for example 01
stops.summary: A larger level in six areas, each built for one enemy and flowing into the next: a lantern clearing with the ball pit and the dummy, a broken aqueduct, a waterfall ravine, an ember hollow, an iron mine open to the sky and a troll bridge, with ambience, autosaves and area names; shots ricochet off iron and pass through wood.
stops.note: Level C since the owner's direction of 2026-10-22: the kit's projectiles meet walls by their layers (bounce, pass, end). If Phase 6 runs long, the feature gate may move it to 1.x (D-194), that surface with it. Records a frame-time capture for C1.

stops.label: 01 (e) fixes
stops.title: Fixes from the playtest
stops.summary: The held spells' frame-time collapse fixed and the full pit's per-ball systems trimmed; the frost crawler that never attacks, the troll that never freezes, damage numbers that wait, lightning that stops at the cursor, the mana readout, stacking area titles and a faint bloom; halved spell costs and doubled regeneration; the lantern now a staff light that burns mana, which crawlers visibly fear; three seconds of play after death.
stops.note: From the owner's playtest notes of 2026-10-21 (example-01-feedback.md). No public API. Opus max by its own tier (D-195), as it draws the crawler's fear and synthesizes sounds.

stops.label: 01 (f) feel
stops.title: Feel: knockback, effects and sounds
stops.summary: Pushes, missiles and iron knock enemies back; several longer black holes that also sweep up small balls; weightier iron that splats what it kills and fizzles where it won't fit; blood, bleeding, burning and a building chill; a fiercer flamethrower drawn above the enemies; a nine-round gun reloaded on R; and the sounds every action was missing.
stops.note: From the owner's playtest notes of 2026-10-21 (example-01-feedback.md). No public API. Opus max by its own tier (D-195).

stops.label: 01 (g) props and foes
stops.title: Props and foes
stops.summary: Crates that catch fire and burn up, powder kegs that set each other off, a goblin that throws rocks and, one throw in five, a fused bomb, and a quicker troll with a fast swipe, placed on the new level and offered by the summon slot.
stops.note: From the owner's playtest notes of 2026-10-21 (example-01-feedback.md). No public API. Opus max by its own tier (D-195).

stops.label: 01 (h) the look
stops.title: The look
stops.summary: A wizard with a big hat whose staff tip is the light, with spell animations; one icon family; fluid health and mana bars and an action bar showing each spell's key; 01's own darker, blue-tinged theme with purple accents; a starry title screen.
stops.note: From the owner's playtest notes of 2026-10-21 (example-01-feedback.md). No template change: 01's own colours over the template's theme. Opus max by its own tier (D-195).

stops.label: Phase 6 QA pass
stops.title: Phase 6 audit
stops.summary: The same audit for Phase 6, plus W8b: the shader ID allocator, queued transitions and the remaining P3s.

stops.title: Feature gate
stops.summary: You play the acceptance game start to finish from its packaged archive, built only on the public API and the kit. You also settle platform tiers and the minimum audio and physics features.

stops.label: C1
stops.title: Benchmarks and budgets
stops.summary: A dated 1.0 baseline with new rows for UI, text, startup, a game frame, hierarchy, kit systems and tuple queries. Each row gets a budget.
stops.note: Budgets are set at the feature gate (Q12, at its default). Fixes that need an API change land now.

stops.label: W4b
stops.title: API freeze
stops.summary: Break ledger emptied, arity-named queries removed, #[non_exhaustive] sweep, missing_docs clean, rustdoc examples, an API snapshot.

stops.title: Freeze gate
stops.summary: You confirm the public API is final and decide on crates.io.

stops.label: C2
stops.title: Performance pass
stops.summary: Rows over budget are fixed, largest gap first, with no API changes.

stops.label: W7b, W9b and W9c
stops.title: Platforms and the getting-started guide
stops.summary: Support tiers in the README, a macOS build if you choose one, the getting-started guide's final pass, crates.io if you chose it.
stops.note: Your check: runs on Windows and macOS machines, if you have them.

stops.title: RC gate
stops.summary: Every budget passes or has an exception you accepted, and the first release candidate is tagged.

stops.label: C3
stops.title: Release candidates
stops.summary: Each candidate runs the full release checklist, ending with your playthrough. A failure is fixed and a new candidate tagged.

stops.title: Tungsten 1.0
stops.summary: Every row of the release checklist passed or accepted, and the tag is cut.

questions.text: Which definition of 1.0, is an acceptance game the test, and what game is it?
questions.default: A and B (complete for making games, stable library), crates.io left to Q2. One acceptance game: a small top-down action game with a few rooms, a spawner, keys and doors, a boss room and a save slot
questions.answer: A and B; one acceptance game: a top-down survivors-like auto-shooter (D-102), whose pitch, screens and mechanics were agreed on 2026-10-05 (acceptance-game.md)

questions.text: wgpu and winit types in the stable API: hide them, tier them, or accept their majors?
questions.default: Hide them: a curated umbrella re-export, engine-owned input and format types, wgpu-facing Renderer methods behind a handle or a doc(hidden) tier
questions.answer: Hidden from the promise (D-103)

questions.text: UI cut line: broader controls in 1.0? A text field with IME?
questions.default: Sliders, checkboxes and scroll containers in; text fields and IME out
questions.answer: Sliders and checkboxes in as W1 BC; text fields and IME out

questions.text: Gamepad in 1.0?
questions.default: In: the game plays on a gamepad, and UI navigation needs only bindings
questions.answer: In

questions.text: Save slots in 1.0, or settings only?
questions.default: In: the envelope and listing are small, and C3's playthrough uses a slot
questions.answer: In

questions.text: Kit stability: inside the 1.0 promise, or a tier of its own?
questions.default: Inside the promise, with #[non_exhaustive] on kit settings structs
questions.answer: Inside the promise

questions.text: Multi-core scope: fork-join only (R1, R2), or also a render thread (R4)?
questions.by: Definition gate (proposed); frame-loop gate at the latest
questions.default: R4 moves to 1.x; it returns only if C1 shows a game-frame row over budget that R4 would fix
questions.answer: R2 only: R4 to 1.x at the definition gate (D-102), R1 to 1.x at the frame-loop gate after its spike (D-131)

questions.text: Worker mechanism: std::thread::scope, a rayon pool, or an own pool?
questions.by: Frame-loop gate, after the R1 spike
questions.default: From the R1 spike's verdict
questions.answer: Moot for 1.0: no candidate spawns a worker after R1 left; a rayon pool owned by App if a fork-join stage ever lands (D-131)

questions.text: Require Send + Sync on components and resources before the freeze?
questions.default: From the frame-loop design
questions.answer: No: no Send/Sync bound on components or resources; a parallel path bounds the types it slices at its call site (D-131)

questions.text: Fixed step: physics only, or a fixed-update schedule? Interpolation by default?
questions.default: From the W3 design
questions.answer: A fixed_update stage that takes any system, physics as one plugin's pair in it; interpolation on by default through PrevPosition spawned with the body; at most two steps a frame (D-129)

questions.text: Game clock: which stages keep running on real time while gameplay is paused?
questions.default: From the W3 design
questions.answer: Transitions, the HUD, overlays, the inspector and UI timing on real time; tweens, particles, game feel, the camera and game systems on the game clock; a paused game skips the physics stage (D-129)

questions.text: Logs and crash reports: on by default in App, or one opt-in call?
questions.default: On by default: App::new installs the engine logger unless one is set, and the crash hook where a user folder exists
questions.answer: On by default; a game opts out by setting its own logger first (D-119)

questions.text: Which settings does the engine persist, and does a corrupt user file reset to defaults or stop the game?
questions.default: A corrupt file resets to defaults

questions.text: Minimum audio and physics features for 1.0?
questions.by: W6a starts; the rest at the feature gate
questions.default: Kinematic bodies, sensors and shape queries are Must; the rest cut by the acceptance game
questions.answer: Kinematic bodies, sensors, shape queries, shape and ray casts, layers and masks, audio buses and a voice limit per sound Must; voice handles and fades Should; audio pause 1.x (D-132)

questions.text: Hierarchy: physics bodies on root entities only for 1.0?
questions.default: Yes
questions.answer: Yes, roots only; the acceptance game places its orbiting blades each fixed step (D-132)

questions.text: Controllers: anything beyond ground check, coyote time, jump buffer and variable jump?
questions.default: Nothing beyond those four; slopes, one-way platforms and ladders go to the backlog
questions.answer: Nothing beyond those four; slopes, one-way platforms and ladders in the 1.x backlog (D-158)

questions.text: CLI tiers, and argument parsing and archive writing by hand or by crate?
questions.default: check and package Must, new Should
questions.answer: check and package Must, new Should, all three landed; arguments by hand, archives with the platform's tar (D-182)

questions.text: Platform tiers and a macOS release build?
questions.default: Linux certified, other platforms on stated tiers as far as hosts allow; no macOS release build for 1.0

questions.text: Publish the library crates on crates.io for 1.0?
